title: LaFiSe BAnK Pocket
overview: DISCOVER AND IDEATION — USER TESTING RESEARCH · MVP Design Plan

sections.label: WHAT THE BUSINESS WANTED TO VALIDATE

items.title: Digital Payment Hypotheses
items.body: Validate core assumptions about merchant payment behaviour — whether entrepreneurs prefer digital solutions over traditional POS terminals and why.

items.title: User Language & Priorities
items.body: Understand the mental model and vocabulary of small business owners when interacting with financial apps. Surface unmet needs and latent desires.

items.title: Competitive Bias
items.body: Identify expectations and biases shaped by prior experiences with competitor apps (WhatsApp Pay, Yappy) to inform differentiated positioning.

methods.label: Test Format
methods.body: Moderated usability testing with think-aloud protocol. Conducted remotely and in-person across Costa Rica and Panama.

methods.label: User Groups
methods.body: Young Professionals (22–30), Mid-Career (31–45), University Students (18–22), Senior Users (55+), Unbanked Merchants.

methods.label: Prototype
methods.body: High-fidelity clickable Figma prototype covering 5 core flows: Onboarding, Transfer, Payment Request, Dashboard, Account Settings.

methods.label: Metrics Captured
methods.body: Task completion rate, time-on-task, error rate, SUS score, NPS, and qualitative insights.

methods.label: Recording
methods.body: Screen + audio recording with consent. Sessions transcribed and tagged using affinity mapping.

methods.label: Analysis Method
methods.body: Rainbow spreadsheet analysis, SUS scoring per group, priority severity matrix (impact × frequency).

items.title: Navigation Confusion
items.body: Couldn't locate 'Request Payment' without guidance. Tab labels were ambiguous — users expected task-based language, not category names.

items.title: Transfer Friction
items.body: 7-step transfer flow created overload. 70% expected fewer taps, influenced by WhatsApp Pay. Fee disclosure only appeared at step 6.

items.title: Auth Overload
items.body: Biometric + PIN + OTP felt excessive. Senior users (55+) abandoned authentication in 40% of cases.

items.title: Error Handling
items.body: Generic error messages caused anxiety. 55% abandoned after first error screen with no clear recovery path visible.

items.title: Dashboard Clarity
items.body: Balance visibility praised by 80% of users. Transaction list was clear and familiar — strongest-performing section and a validated foundation.

quadrants.title: Quick Wins
items: Add text to bottom bar icons

items.title: IA Redefinition
items.body: Mi Pocket and Mi Cuenta are now the main tab bar entry points. Profile moved to top-right. Invoices and charges become primary CTAs. Smart filters for complex data search.

items.title: Tab Bar Redesign
items.body: Mi Pocket and Mi Cuenta are now the two main tab bar entry points. Persistent text labels added below all icons for clarity.

items.title: Smart Auth Tiers
items.body: Biometric-only for transfers under $50. PIN + biometric for $50–$500. Full OTP for amounts above $500. Risk-proportional security.

items.title: App Tour
items.body: An app tour was created to facilitate user onboarding across the main app features — reducing confusion on first launch.

items.title: Transfer Flow 7→4 Steps
items.body: Consolidated recipient selection + amount + fee disclosure into a single smart screen. Confirmation simplified to one tap.

items.title: UI Redesign & Real Estate Optimisation
items.body: Tiered membership UI with clear perks per level. Gamification mechanics ('earn & spend') added to transaction confirmations.

sections.label: REFLECTION
sections.content: Designing Poket taught me that financial inclusion isn't just about features — it's about trust. Every extra authentication step, every ambiguous label, every generic error message erodes confidence in a product that holds people's money. The SUS score of 62.5 was a clear signal: the data we needed to redesign with purpose. Seeing merchants across Costa Rica and Panama use a simpler, faster product is what the work was really about.
